title: Making Conjugation-induced Fluorescent PEGylated Virus-like Particles by Dibromomaleimide-disulfide Chemistry
protocol: Prepare Lysogeny broth (LB) agar and pour plates.
Transform BL21(DE3) with a pET28 plasmid containing the wtQβ coat protein sequence.
Thaw E. coli BL21(DE3) competent cells in an ice bath.
Place 50 μL of cells in a microcentrifuge tube.
Add 2 μL of plasmid into one tube and gently flick the tube.
Incubate on ice for 30 min.
Heat-shock the cells for 45 s in a water bath at exactly 42 °C.
Place the tube back in the ice bath immediately after heat-shocking, and incubate for 5 min.
Add 950 μL of LB media without any antibiotic.
Shake the culture at 200 rpm for 60 min at 37 °C.
Plate 100 μL of the culture on LB agar plates with Kanamycin.
Incubate the plate overnight at 37 °C.
Select white colonies when needed.
Make Super Optimal Broth (SOB) media.
Autoclave two 2 L baffled Erlenmeyer flasks on a superdry cycle.
Weigh out and add 20.0 g of tryptone, 5.0 g of yeast extract, 2.469 g of anhydrous magnesium sulfate, 0.584 g of sodium chloride, and 0.186 g of potassium chloride to each flask.
Bring the volume to 1 L with ultrapure water in each flask and autoclave on the liquid cycle.
Once the SOB media has reached room temperature after autoclaving, add 1 mL of kanamycin (100 mg/mL) to each liter of media.
Store at 4 °C.
Make 0.1 M potassium phosphate buffer (pH 7.00).
Dissolve 68.045 g of potassium monobasic in 500 mL of ultrapure water to make 1 M potassium monobasic solution.
Make 1 M potassium dibasic solution by dissolving 87.09 g of potassium dibasic in 500 mL of ultrapure water.
Add 38.5 mL of potassium monobasic solution and 61.5 mL of potassium dibasic to a 1 L bottle.
Adjust pH to 7.00 if needed, and bring to a volume of 1 L.
Make 5–40% sucrose gradients in 0.1 M potassium phosphate buffer (pH 7.00).
Prepare solutions with 5–40% (increasing in increments of 5%) sucrose dissolved in 0.1 M potassium phosphate buffer (pH 7.00) in 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Deposit 3.3 mL of 5% sucrose solution at the bottom of a 38 mL round-bottom polycarbonate tube using a long needle syringe and repeat this for five other tubes.
Carefully deposit 3.3 mL of 10% sucrose solution at the bottom of the tube, and carefully remove the needle as to not disturb the gradient.
Repeat for the other five tubes.
Continue to deposit 3.3 mL layers of sucrose solutions, increasing from 15% to 40% in each tube, while being cautious to not disturb the gradient.
Cover the tops of the gradients with foil and store at -80 °C.
Wipe bench area with 1:1 bleach/ethanol.
Make two 3 mL starter cultures by adding single colonies of E. coli BL21(DE3) into 3 mL of SOB media in an aseptic environment.
Grow on a shaker at 250 rpm in a 37 °C and 0% relative humidity (rH) room overnight.
Inoculate starter culture in SOB media.
Take both 3 mL starter cultures off the shaker.
Pour each starter culture into one of two 2 L baffled Erlenmeyer flasks with 1 L of fresh SOB media in each.
Place the inoculated media on a shaker at 250 rpm in a 37 °C and 0% rH room.
Grow bacteria on the shaker until OD600 reaches 0.9–1.0.
Add 1 mL of 1 M IPTG to induce protein expression using a P1000 pipette.
Leave media on the shaker overnight at 250 rpm in a 37 °C and 0% rH room.
Remove media from the shaker the following morning.
Centrifuge media using 1000 mL bottles at 20,621 × g for 1 h at 4 °C to harvest cells.
Discard supernatant and collect cell pellet.
Pour supernatant into a flask with about 5 mL of bleach to kill bacteria.
Use a spatula to scrape the cell pellet from the bottom of the centrifuge bottle.
Put the cell pellet into a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Resuspend cell pellet with ~20–30 mL of 0.1 M potassium phosphate buffer (pH 7.00).
Lose cells using a microfluidizer processor according to manufacturer’s protocol.
Centrifuge lysate in 250 mL centrifuge bottles at 20,621 x g for 1 hr at 4 °C.
Discard the pellet.
Measure the volume of supernatant in mL.
Multiply that value by 0.265 and add an equivalent amount of g of ammonium sulfate to the supernatant.
Stir at 4 °C for at least 1 h on a stir plate at 200 rpm.
Centrifuge in 250 mL bottles at 20,621 x g for 1 h at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with about 10 mL of 0.1 M potassium phosphate buffer (pH 7.00).
Add equal volumes of 1:1 chloroform/n-butanol to the crude sample and mix by vortexing for a few seconds.
Centrifuge in 38 mL tubes at 20,621 × g for 30 minutes at 4 °C.
Recover the top aqueous layer using a Pasteur pipette.
Thaw six 5–40% pre-made sucrose gradients and load about 2 mL of the extract onto each.
Ultracentrifuge at 99,582 x g for 16 h at 4 °C with free deceleration.
Recover particles from blue band visible under LED light using a long needle syringe.
Ultrapellet the recovered particles at 370,541 x g for 2.5 h at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend the transparent pellet of purified particles with 0.1 M potassium phosphate buffer (pH 7.00).
Dissolve 0.0020 g of tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP) into 1 mL of ultrapure water to make a 100x stock solution.
Add 200 µL of Qβ (5 mg/mL) into a microcentrifuge tube.
Follow by adding 20 µL of 100x TCEP stock solution.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 h.
Dissolve 0.0017 g of dibromomaleimide-polyethylene glycol (DB-PEG) in 100 µL of DMF.
Add 680 µL of 10 mM sodium phosphate solution (pH 5.00).
Add reduced Qβ into the DB-PEG solution and observe under a 365 nm UV lamp.
Let the reaction proceed overnight at room temperature on a rotisserie.
Purify the reaction mixture by centrifugal filter three times using 1x PBS at 4 °C.
Monitor the conjugation by non-reducing SDS-PAGE and native agarose gel electrophoresis.
